Class Ascii

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.gaia.core.text.Ascii
public final class Ascii extends Object
Classes, case mapping, comparison and trimming of ASCII characters, as many protocols, file formats and identifiers define them. 
Ascii.equalsIgnoreCase("DocType", "DOCTYPE")  // true
Ascii.equalsIgnoreCase("PUBLıC", "PUBLIC")    // false
Ascii.toLowerCase("Text/HTML")                // text/html
Ascii.strip("\r\n utf-8\t")                   // utf-8

Only the 26 letters A to Z and a to z have a case here: every other character is left as it is. Unlike String.equalsIgnoreCase(String) or String.toLowerCase(java.util.Locale), these methods never match or turn ı (U+0131), ſ (U+017F) or the Kelvin sign (U+212A) into i, s or k, and never depend on the default locale.

The methods that take a code point accept a char, which widens to it, and any int: one that is no code point is in no class, and is returned unchanged. The methods that take text return a String: the text's CharSequence.toString() itself if they change nothing, without copying it.

Since:
0.1.2

      public static boolean regionMatchesIgnoreCase(CharSequence text, int offset, CharSequence other)
      Returns whether a region of a text, starting at an offset and as long as another text, equals that other text, ignoring ASCII case.
      Parameters:
      text - the text
      offset - the index in text where the region starts
      other - the text to compare the region with
      Returns:
      whether the region equals other ignoring ASCII case; false if it would run past the end of text, and true for an empty other at an offset up to the length of text
      Throws:
      IndexOutOfBoundsException - if offset is negative
